answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with unique storage proofs. Each identity must continuously hold a large, unique dataset derived from its own key, verified by unpredictable spot-checks. Storage cannot be shared, because each identity's data is different, and it cannot be rented on demand, because spot-checks arrive without warning. Like an island's pigment on a reef, each identity's data is distinct and visible. Each extra fake needs its own terabyte of unique, always-on storage, a cost that cannot be shared, parallelized, or bought in bulk.
